Countries

Where we work

Satellite-based surveys are available in Mozambique, South Africa and Nigeria, with no site visit and no drone flight. Drone surveys are available subject to the permits and authorisations each job requires, which differ in each country.

As of 26 September 2026

What applies in each country

A short orientation to the land rules our registers are measured against and the drone rules that shape a survey plan. It summarises public rules for information and is not legal advice; the sources are linked.

Português · English

Mozambique

Land. The Land Law makes the land within 50 m on each side of oil, gas, water, electricity and telecommunications lines a partial protection zone, where no land-use right (DUAT) can be acquired, only special licences (Lei n.º 19/97, arts. 8 and 9). The Electricity Law sets a servitude of up to 50 m from a line’s axis (Lei n.º 12/2022, art. 43).

Drones. Flights are regulated by the civil aviation authority (IACM). Aerial surveys also need authorisation under Lei n.º 6/2024, de 4 de Junho, including for handing the survey data to the client (art. 13).

English

South Africa

Land. Pipelines, power lines and bulk-water lines run in servitudes, and servitude diagrams are the work of registered professional land surveyors. Our registers support that work; they are not cadastral surveys.

Drones. Commercial drone work needs an operator certificate (UASOC) from the South African Civil Aviation Authority and an Air Service Licence (Civil Aviation Regulations Part 101, GN R.3170, 2023).

English

Nigeria

Land. The Oil Pipelines Act lets buildings and cultivation be restricted within a set distance, not exceeding 100 feet, of a pipeline’s licensed land (s.12). Power-line rights of way are set by voltage in the NESIS Regulations 2015, from 11 m to 50 m, with no structures under the line (NESIS).

Drones. Commercial drone work needs an RPAS Operator Certificate from the NCAA, with security clearance built into the process (Nig.CARs 2023 Part 21).

Drone permits and AfriScan

We never assume a permit. Afridrone is working towards the operator approvals each country requires, and every drone proposal sets out the permits and authorisations that particular flight needs and how they fit the schedule. Satellite-based work involves no drone flight.

Language

Reports in English or Portuguese

Reports are available in English or Portuguese. Country pages for Mozambique (in Portuguese and English), South Africa and Nigeria set out the protection zones, servitude rules, procurement routes and drone regulations that apply in each, with sources and review dates.

The methodology and imagery and data sources are the same in every country.

Know what stands inside your right of way, before it becomes a dispute.

Send us your route or site boundary and the distances that matter to you. We reply with a scope, an imagery plan and a written proposal.
